# What hosted CI actually checks, and what it does not.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. .github/workflows/build.yml produces five green checks
# on every commit to main. A reader who sees five green checks reasonably
# concludes the commit was fully verified. It was not: the test suite never runs
# hosted. Nothing anywhere said so in a form a machine could check, so the gap
# was invisible to exactly the person the checks exist to inform — someone who
# does not trust this machine and is reading the commit on GitHub.
#
# This file is the declared coverage, and tools/lint/check_verification_coverage.sh
# holds it to the workflow. It cannot drift: every item claiming to be hosted
# must name a job key that really exists in build.yml, and every job in build.yml
# must be claimed by some item. Adding a job without declaring what it verifies
# fails lint; claiming an item is hosted when its job was renamed or deleted
# fails lint.
#
# THE FIVE ITEMS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE HERE. The gate hard-codes the required item
# list (gcc, clang, lint, tests, fuzz-replay) in its own file, so the gap cannot
# be closed by deleting a row. That two files must agree is the point — the same
# discipline check_promotion_receipt_chain.sh prong 6 documents, added there
# after a mutation reworded a message and a same-file self-test still passed.
#
# Format — five `|`-separated fields, one item per line:
#
#   item | hosted | job_key | display_name | attested_by
#
#   item          short name of the verification item.
#   hosted        exactly `yes` or `no`. Nothing else parses.
#   job_key       the YAML key under `jobs:` in build.yml when hosted=yes;
#                 exactly `-` when hosted=no. NOT the display name: matrix job
#                 names are templated (`compile-check (${{ matrix.cc }})`) and
#                 never appear literally in the file, so a display-name match
#                 would be checking a string that is not there.
#   display_name  the check name a reader sees on GitHub, for humans only.
#   attested_by   where the verdict comes from when hosted=no. Must be
#                 non-empty; `-` when hosted=yes. An item that is not hosted and
#                 does not say who vouches for it is an unverified claim.
#
# CONFIRMATION STATUS — read this before quoting any row as verified.
#
# The gcc, clang, lint, fuzz-replay and compile-all-tus rows were each confirmed
# against a real check-run attached to commit df752afce on origin/main (run
# 30509201499, all five success).
#
# The `tests` row is NEWLY hosted and is NOT yet confirmed by any successful
# check-run. `hosted=yes` here means only what the gate can check — that a job
# with that key exists in build.yml and this file claims it. It does NOT mean
# the job has ever gone green. The job is a deliberate first measurement of two
# things nobody in this repo has measured: whether a hosted runner can carry
# this suite at all, and how much of the corpus silently assumes the maintainer
# host (a live node, a legacy zclassicd datadir, a populated ~/.zclassic-c23 —
# a runner has none of them).
#
# If that first run comes back red or times out, the honest resolutions are to
# fix the coupling, or to declare a smaller hosted scope in this file and say
# what is excluded and why. The dishonest resolutions — which this project has
# already been burned by and which are therefore ruled out here — are trimming
# the corpus until it passes, gating on a narrow tail/grep instead of the full
# output, or leaving this paragraph asserting a confirmation that never happened.
# Replace this block with a run id and a verdict once one exists either way.

gcc|yes|compile-check|compile-check (gcc)|-
clang|yes|compile-check|compile-check (clang)|-
lint|yes|lint|lint (make lint)|-
fuzz-replay|yes|fuzz-replay|fuzz-replay (saved findings)|-
compile-all-tus|yes|build|build (cached dependencies)|-
tests|yes|tests|tests (make test-parallel)|-
